about.what: The multisig family registry (exo-68f). One entry per FAMILY — a way a group can hold an account and authorize from it, or (the `each` locus, docs/design/split-the-bill.md) a way a group agrees who pays what with no account at all — across chains. A family is scheme x settlement x profile (docs/design/multisig-landscape.md §5). A DRIVER implements a family; an ACCOUNT is a family instantiated (chain, address/descriptor, signer set, policy). Checked by scripts/check-family-registry.py.
about.honesty: Every non-room entry names a primary source. Anything not confirmed from a primary source is listed under `unverified` on the entry, never folded into the fields. Muster classifies families; it never scores or ranks them for the user.

locus.native: the protocol itself checks the account/script policy
locus.contract: a contract/program verifies signatures collected off-chain, in one transaction
locus.vote: each approver sends their own on-chain transaction; the chain counts
locus.aggregate: signers combine off-chain into one ordinary signature; the chain sees a single signer
locus.room: no chain: the room's own log is where agreement is final
locus.each: no shared account: the room agrees who owes what, and each party settles their own part with their own transaction; nothing on a chain counts or enforces the agreement

scheme.shared-bytes: every signer signs the same bytes
scheme.per-signer-bytes: each signer signs a slightly different blob (e.g. their own account id appended)
scheme.own-transaction: each approval is the approver's own transaction
scheme.aggregate-n-of-n: partial signatures over shared bytes combine into one; every key must take part
scheme.aggregate-threshold: partial signatures from any t of n combine into one

commits.content: the signature covers the full action
commits.pointer: the approval covers only an index / address / hash that POINTS at the action stored elsewhere

binding.explicit: the chain-signed bytes carry a chain/network id
binding.implicit: bound through something that only exists on that chain (UTXO, blockhash, object version)
binding.none: the chain-signed bytes are valid on another network of the same chain
binding.room: no chain signature — muster's envelope is the only binding

ordering.sequence: one strict counter: a stuck action blocks every later one
ordering.utxo: actions conflict only when they spend the same coins
ordering.objects: actions conflict when they touch the same object versions
ordering.dedup: no ordering; replay stopped by id dedup / leases

expiry.optional: the family supports an expiry the proposer may set
expiry.forced: the chain forces a short validity window (see expiryWindow)

setup.none: nothing to set up (the room roster is the signer set)
setup.derive: the address is derived from the keys + policy; nothing on-chain until first use
setup.register: an on-chain transaction registers the signer set on an existing account
setup.dkg: an interactive key-generation ceremony among the signers

membershipChange.in-place: change signers/threshold on the same address (itself an approved action)
membershipChange.new-address: a new account; funds must be moved (sweep)
membershipChange.reshare: a key ceremony re-deals shares; the address is kept

reveal.never: an outside observer never learns this

effectVisibility.public: the action's contents are public on settle
effectVisibility.shielded: the action's contents stay private on-chain
effectVisibility.room-only: the action never leaves the room
effectVisibility.target-module: the room agrees, then the action is handed to the Logos module it names; that module's own disclosure applies

approverCost.per-signature: each extra signature raises the one fee
approverCost.per-vote: each approval is a transaction the approver pays for
approverCost.per-vote-deposit: each approval is a paid transaction and someone locks a deposit

status.built: a driver exists and passes conformance
status.partial: a driver exists but is a subset/scaffold (see why)
status.watch: fits in principle; blocked on maturity, license, or scope

families.name: Room threshold (k of the members)
families.signs: dCBOR [domain, schemaId, fields] of the effect; muster's signing envelope commits to environment/account/slot/expiry

muster.why: the room roster (Ed25519 encryption identities) is the signer set; 'unanimous' is the k=n variant

families.name: Signed statement (EIP-191 personal_sign)
families.signs: keccak256("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n" + len + dCBOR effect)

muster.why: a group statement any EVM tool can verify; settles nothing

families.name: Room-agreed module action (invoke)
families.signs: dCBOR [domain, schemaId = muster.invoke.<module>.<method>.v1, args] — two methods never share signable bytes
infra: the named Logos module, loaded on this host
families.notes: What the called module does next (e.g. lez_core sending on the LEZ) is that module's own disclosure, carried on the manifest's target-module rows.

muster.why: any Logos module action under a room threshold (driver derivation, exo-fa4)

families.name: Two-round FROST-shaped room policy
families.signs: dCBOR effect, once per round (no Schnorr aggregation)

muster.why: exercises the multi-round seam; its own header says it is a coordination scaffold, not production FROST. Superseded by the aggregate families below.

families.name: Safe (v1.4.1 / v1.5.0)
families.signs: EIP-712 safeTxHash: domain(chainId, verifyingContract=Safe) + SafeTx(to, value, data, operation, safeTxGas, baseGas, gasPrice, gasToken, refundReceiver, nonce)
bypasses: modules (execTransactionFromModule skips the threshold)
AllowanceModule delegates
operation=delegatecall runs arbitrary code in the Safe's context (the Bybit vector)
families.notes: Safe <=1.2.0 has no chainId in the domain (binding none). v=1 'approved hash' is an on-chain pre-approval visible before execution. Same CREATE2 address on every chain unless created chain-specific.

muster.why: accounts are disclosed by members into the room (exo-a50.1.3); every SafeTx field reaches the signed hash, delegatecall is shown and refused unless allowlisted, modules and guard are read from chain, and it settles through the settlement seam (profile-chosen, assembled from the log, submitted by a configured relayer through the EVM adapter) against the real Safe v1.4.1 — verified equal to its getTransactionHash (exo-a50.1.4, exo-a50.1.5).

families.name: Safe via Safe4337Module (ERC-4337)
families.signs: EIP-712 SafeOp(safe, nonce, initCode, callData, gas fields, paymasterAndData, validAfter, validUntil, entryPoint); domain verifyingContract = the module, not the Safe
bypasses: as evm.safe
families.notes: The EntryPoint 2D nonce is a second replay domain beside the Safe nonce. EntryPoint v0.7 only.

muster.why: same account as evm.safe with a different settlement path; worth it once gas sponsorship matters

families.name: ERC-7579 account + OwnableValidator (Rhinestone)
families.signs: EIP-191 personal_sign of the userOpHash (userOpHash commits to entryPoint + chainid)
bypasses: other installed validators/executors on the modular account
families.notes: Hardware wallets see only an opaque hash (blind signing). Max 32 owners. No validity window: OwnableValidator.validateUserOp returns only 0 (valid) or 1 (invalid), so validUntil is 0, which ERC-4337 reads as never expiring; collected owner signatures stay valid until the UserOp's nonce is used. A window could only come from outside the validator (a paymaster's validationData, or another module on the account).

muster.why: the modular-account path; blind signing makes muster's re-derived review the only human-readable view

families.name: ZeroDev Kernel v3 WeightedECDSAValidator
families.signs: N-1 guardians sign EIP-712 Approve(keccak(sender, callData, nonce)) — no gas/paymaster fields; the last signs EIP-191(userOpHash)
bypasses: once Approved, a userOp with a non-zero paymaster passes with no guardian signature

muster.why: the approval does not cover gas/paymaster, and the verified source shows a paymaster path around the guardians

families.name: EOA delegated to multisig logic (EIP-7702)
families.signs: whatever the delegate verifies; the delegation itself is keccak(0x05 || rlp([chain_id, address, nonce])) and chain_id 0 is valid everywhere
bypasses: the EOA's own key can always act alone and re-delegate

muster.why: the threshold is advisory: the root key can never be removed, so muster could not honestly call it a multisig

families.name: Gnosis MultiSigWallet (legacy)
families.signs: each owner's own transaction calling confirmTransaction(id)
bypasses: ...WithDailyLimit lets one owner send ETH up to the limit

muster.why: archived 2021; import read-only at most

families.name: Bitcoin P2WSH sortedmulti (descriptor + PSBT)
families.signs: BIP-143 sighash per input: outpoint, the full witnessScript (so the policy), THIS input's amount only, nSequence, hashOutputs, locktime
families.notes: Signatures never expire: revoking means double-spending an input. The fee is implicit (BIP-143 commits only to the signer's own input amount) — every signer must re-derive it from the prevouts. PSBT bytes are not canonical. A fee bump is a new signing round. Keycard Shell 1.4 cosigns P2WSH multisig and stores descriptors.

muster.why: a member discloses the account (k of n keys; the address is re-derived, so the disclosure is checked without a chain read) and proposes a spend built from the UTXOs their own node reports (an external read the log records, invariant 10); every input's BIP-143 hash is re-derived; a member signs in-app through the keystore (DER, attested by the same key, exo-a50.2.4); a signer outside muster signs the exported PSBT and the imported signature counts, shown as signed outside muster (exo-a50.2.6); the Bitcoin settlement finalizes the witnesses and the bitcoind adapter broadcasts and watches confirmations (exo-a50.2.5). Verified end to end against Bitcoin Core v31.1 on regtest (btc_regtest_e2e): Core derives the same address, its wallet signs muster's PSBT, and it accepts muster's witnesses.

families.name: Bitcoin taproot tapscript multi_a / sortedmulti_a
families.signs: BIP-341 SigMsg (all inputs' amounts and scriptPubKeys) + the BIP-342 tapleaf hash
families.notes: Only the executed leaf is revealed; unused leaves stay hidden. Commits to all inputs' amounts, which closes P2WSH's implicit-fee hole. Sparrow rejects taproot script trees.

muster.why: the same driver and path for a single sortedmulti_a leaf under the NUMS internal key: BIP-341/342 script-path hashes (committing to every input's amount), BIP-340 signatures in-app through the keystore or imported from an outside signer's PSBT (BIP-371 fields), witnesses finalized one slot per key with the leaf and control block. Verified end to end against Bitcoin Core v31.1 on regtest (btc_regtest_e2e) alongside P2WSH — the two cards read the same row for row: at spend both reveal the policy and the signers.

unverified: which BIP-48-style path convention wallets use for taproot multisig

families.name: Bitcoin miniscript with timelocked recovery (e.g. Liana)
families.signs: BIP-143 (wsh) or BIP-341/342 (tr). In tr a script-path signature commits to its tapleaf hash, so it is valid only on the leaf (path) it was made for. In wsh it commits to the whole witnessScript, every branch included, so the signature does not fix the path. older(n) / after(n) are met through the signed nSequence / nLockTime
bypasses: the recovery path becomes spendable by fewer keys after its timelock — by design
families.notes: wsh reveals the whole policy including recovery branches; tr reveals only the executed leaf (nothing on a key-path spend). Relative timelocks (older(), the only kind Liana supports) restart when coins are spent back to the account ('refresh'); absolute ones (after(), as in Bitcoin Core's decaying-multisig example) open at a fixed height and cannot be refreshed, and moving them needs a new descriptor. In wsh a primary-path spend must keep nSequence below the recovery lock, or the recovery branch could complete it with fewer signatures. BIP-379 is Draft but deployed.

muster.why: a second policy shape (decaying threshold) on the same Bitcoin settlement; the card needs a 'path' slot

families.name: Bitcoin taproot MuSig2 (key path)
families.signs: BIP-341 key-path SigMsg under the tweaked aggregate key
families.notes: n-of-n only (BIP-327): k-of-n needs one aggregate per k-subset. Reusing a secret nonce leaks the key — nonce state must be marked consumed before sharing. Any tx change (RBF) needs a fresh nonce round from all n.

muster.why: the simplest aggregate; useful as the key path over a tapscript fallback

families.name: Bitcoin taproot FROST (BIP-445 + ChillDKG)
families.signs: BIP-341 key-path SigMsg; each partial signature is also bound to the signer set and aggregate nonce
families.notes: ChillDKG needs authenticated host keys and a relaying coordinator, and aborts on faults (not robust). Resharing is not specified. Frostsnap ships a FROST taproot product.

muster.why: the flagship: true t-of-n that looks single-sig, and the room is exactly the authenticated coordinator ChillDKG asks for. Built and held to Phase D's exit on a real Bitcoin Core (phase_d_exit_test): the ChillDKG ceremony over the room's log (every member computes the coordinator's steps; the account is disclosed with its public recovery data), round secrets as keystore operations (S7: shares recovered from the recovery data, never stored; nonces consumed before use; a restart aborts), the two rounds with the signer set fixed by the log, and a key-path spend whose witness is one BIP-340 signature — Core's rawtr(x(Q)), indistinguishable from a single-sig spend. Hosted and in the room UI: open/join a ceremony, the BTC composer, Approve once (round 2 follows). Demo-grade (not constant time), behind the production gate.

unverified: whether Frostsnap matches the BIP-445 test vectors

families.name: Squads v4 (Solana)
families.signs: each approver's own transaction pointing at the Proposal PDA (multisig, transaction_index); the payload is stored on-chain, immutable after creation
families.expiryWindow: each vote transaction's blockhash lives ~60-90s; the proposal itself persists
bypasses: spending limits bypass the threshold and can be granted to non-members
a config authority (controlled mode)
a stale vault transaction that was already approved can still execute
families.notes: Time lock up to 3 months after approval. Adding or removing a member, or changing the threshold or time lock (and, on a controlled multisig, the config authority), makes every earlier transaction stale; adding or removing a spending limit or setting the rent collector does not. The mainnet program has no upgrade authority (immutable since slot 302,582,236).

muster.why: the reference vote-locus family; approvals point at on-chain content, so muster must read and re-derive it before every approval

families.name: Squads Smart Account (Solana, 2026)
families.signs: the whole Solana message (sync mode: all signers co-sign one transaction)
families.expiryWindow: blockhash ~60-90s unless a durable nonce is used
bypasses: policies

muster.why: mainnet since 2026-04; the sync mode is the room-collected shape muster wants on Solana

families.name: SPL Token native multisig
families.signs: the whole message: header, account keys, recent_blockhash or durable nonce, instructions
families.expiryWindow: blockhash ~60-90s; a durable nonce is single-use and anything advancing it kills every collected signature

muster.why: covers token authorities only, 1-11 signers, no update instruction

families.name: SPL Governance / Realms
families.signs: each vote is its own transaction

muster.why: token-weighted DAO governance, not a multisig; upstream archived (maintained by Mythic)

families.name: Cosmos SDK x/auth multisig (LegacyAminoPubKey)
families.signs: LEGACY_AMINO_JSON AminoSignDoc{account_number, chain_id, sequence, timeout_height, memo, msgs, fee, ...} of the multisig account (DIRECT unsupported by multisign; TEXTUAL removed in v0.55)
bypasses: an x/authz grant the account made (MsgGrant, itself signed k of n): the grantee then sends the granted message types for the account alone (MsgExec) until the grant expires or is revoked
an x/feegrant allowance the account made (MsgGrantAllowance, k of n): the grantee's transaction fees are paid from the account, up to the allowance
interop: unsigned tx JSON + per-member signature JSON (tx multisign)
families.notes: The address changes with membership and even key order. Any other tx from the account voids collected signatures. Default TxSigLimit 7 counts all n keys, so a 3-of-8 cannot transact on default params.

muster.why: clean shared-bytes family; the sequence-voids-signatures rule is exactly what the ordering slot must show

families.name: Cosmos x/group
families.signs: each member's MsgVote
families.expiryWindow: voting period, then max execution period
bypasses: the group admin

muster.why: moved out of core in v0.54 under a Source Available Evaluation License; production use needs a Cosmos Enterprise license

families.name: CosmWasm cw3 multisig / DAO DAO
families.signs: each voter's MsgExecuteContract Vote{proposal_id}

muster.why: cw-plus is unaudited per its README; DAO DAO is active — a second vote-locus candidate if Cosmos demand appears

families.name: Polkadot/Substrate pallet-multisig (+ pure proxy)
families.signs: approvers: approve_as_multi{threshold, other_signatories, timepoint, call_hash} (never executes, even at k); execution: as_multi with the full call, sent by any signatory once k approvals are in (its own counted if still needed). Each extrinsic commits to genesis hash, spec/tx version, era, the sender's nonce, metadata hash
bypasses: proxies (by design, for a stable address)
families.notes: The first approver locks a deposit and is the only one who can cancel. A runtime change can change what a call hash decodes to: the Asset Hub migration did not carry pending multisig operations over (their approvals were lost and must be re-announced on Asset Hub; deposits were unlocked). The call stays a hash on-chain until a signatory submits it with as_multi.

muster.why: the room is the natural carrier for the call data the chain only sees as a hash

families.name: XRP Ledger SignerList
families.signs: "SMT\0" + tx (empty SigningPubKey) + THAT signer's AccountID — each signer signs a different blob
bypasses: the master key and a regular key each still sign alone beside the signer list: the list can remove the regular key, but only a master-key-signed AccountSet can disable the master key (multi-signed, it fails tecNEED_MASTER_KEY), so that bypass closes only if the master-key holder closes it
families.notes: On networks with id <= 1024 (mainnet 0, testnet 1, devnet 2) a NetworkID field is refused (telNETWORK_ID_MAKES_TX_NON_CANONICAL), so those signatures carry no network binding; above 1024 it is required and must match. Tickets allow out-of-order use. Fee is (N+1) x base.
families.exposure: On XRPL networks with id <= 1024 (mainnet, testnet, devnet) the signed bytes cannot carry a NetworkID: a multi-signed transaction is valid on any of them where the account exists at that Sequence (or holds that Ticket) and its signer list there accepts those signers at quorum. Muster's envelope binds the network in the room (invariant 2); the chain does not - the card must say so.

muster.why: the per-signer-bytes shape: forces the seam to give each contributor their own materialization

unverified: PermissionDelegationV1_1 has held a mainnet majority since 2026-09-24 (not enabled as of ledger 107,292,788); if it holds it activates about 2026-10-08, and a DelegateSet the quorum grants then lets a delegate send the granted transaction types alone — a further bypass

families.name: Stellar weighted signers + thresholds
families.signs: SHA-256(networkId = SHA-256(passphrase) || tagged tx); the tx carries seqNum and preconditions
bypasses: pre-authorized transaction and hash(x) signer types
an ed25519 signed-payload signer (CAP-40): its signature covers a fixed payload, not the transaction, so once produced (public after first use) it adds its weight to any transaction from the account
families.notes: Thresholds are per operation class (low/med/high). Every attached signature must be used: each check (the source's LOW, each operation's class) walks the signatures in envelope order and stops once the weight meets its threshold, so a signature past that point, a duplicate or a non-signer's fails the transaction (txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA) - the order matters, not just the count. A Soroban auth entry signed for the account (address credentials) must name a signatureExpirationLedger at most maxEntryTTL - 1 ledgers ahead (3,110,400 on mainnet, about six months); the transaction's own expiry stays optional.

muster.why: weights + per-operation thresholds exercise the policy slot beyond k-of-n

families.name: Algorand multisig account
families.signs: "TX" || msgpack(txn): commits to genesis hash, first/last valid round, lease, group
families.notes: Key order changes the address. In-place change is via rekey.

muster.why: fits cleanly; no demand signal

families.name: Tron account permissions
families.signs: SHA-256(raw_data) incl. ref_block_hash (the only chain binding), expiration, Permission_id
bypasses: the owner permission can rewrite the active permissions

muster.why: fits; the 24h window is a card countdown

families.name: Hedera KeyList / ThresholdKey
families.signs: TransactionBody: TransactionID (payer + validStart), nodeAccountID, validDuration — no chain/ledger id; SDKs build one body per node, so signers sign N variants
families.expiryWindow: <= 180s (scheduled transactions: up to 62 days, but every approval becomes public)

muster.why: 180s forces the scheduled-transaction path, which turns it into a vote locus

families.name: Sui native MultiSig
families.signs: Blake2b(intent || BCS(TransactionData)); the bytes name the chain only under a ValidDuring expiration (ChainIdentifier, checked by validators; required when gas comes from an address balance and no owned object is an input) - otherwise replay protection is object versions
bypasses: address aliases: each alias is a unilateral full owner
families.notes: Mixed signature schemes in one policy (passkeys, zkLogin). The address is the hash of its policy, but since protocol 116 (live on mainnet) address aliases change signers in place: the address enables aliases and replaces its set with a new MultiSig address, which then signs for it - the address no longer re-derives from its signers, so read its AddressAliases object. Since protocol 124 gas can come from an address balance: a transaction with no owned input then needs a ValidDuring window of at most two epochs that names the chain, and is deduplicated by digest within it rather than ordered by object versions.

muster.why: the richest mixed-signer native policy; tests the signer-kind slot

unverified: whether signing two transactions over the same object version still locks those objects until epoch end: pre-consensus locking has been disabled on mainnet since protocol 105 (owned-object conflicts are detected post-consensus)

families.name: Aptos MultiKey / MultiEd25519
families.signs: SHA3("APTOS::RawTransaction") || BCS(raw tx incl. sequence_number, expiration, chain_id)

muster.why: fits; no demand signal

families.name: Aptos 0x1::multisig_account
families.signs: each owner's vote transaction

muster.why: vote locus; at most 20 pending

families.name: Cardano native scripts (NOfK + timelocks)
families.signs: blake2b-256 of the original tx body bytes: inputs, fee, ttl, validity start, optional network_id, required_signers
bypasses: ledger bug #6086: a negative NOfK threshold is trivially satisfied
families.notes: No CIP for exchanging partially signed transactions (CIP-1854 excludes transport). Hardware wallets need CIP-21 canonical CBOR.

muster.why: fits; the room would be the missing partial-tx transport

families.name: TON multisig v2
families.signs: each signer's wallet message with approve -> the order address; commits only to the order address, not its contents
families.notes: No external-message entry, so signatures cannot be collected off-chain. A config change invalidates every pending order. expiration_date is not checked on approve.

muster.why: vote locus with pointer-only approvals; lower priority than lez.multisig-program

families.name: NEAR multisig contract
families.signs: confirm(request_id) — commits only to the request id

muster.why: old core contracts whose README disclaims guarantees

families.name: Starknet multisig account (Argent/Ready)
families.signs: INVOKE v3 Poseidon tx hash (chain_id + nonce); exactly threshold signatures, sorted by signer GUID
bypasses: guardian escape recovery

muster.why: the vendor (Argent, now Ready) says it is moving to Base

unverified: product status after the Ready rebrand

families.name: ZKsync Era native account abstraction
families.signs: EIP-712 type-113 transaction (domain zkSync/2/chainId; nonce, paymaster, factoryDeps)

muster.why: EraVM retirement announced 2026-09-04; Safe on chain 324 is covered by evm.safe until then

families.name: Zcash FROST for Orchard (shielded)
families.signs: ZIP-244 sighash (consensus_branch_id, expiry_height, actions, anchor, fee) under a re-randomized key; one signing session per spend action
bypasses: every participant holds the full viewing key (sees all activity)
infra: a relay (frostd) — replaced by the room
families.notes: ZIP 312 (Draft): signers MUST check the SIGHASH against the transaction data or compute it themselves; muster always recomputes it (invariant 1). A rogue coordinator can break unlinkability. nExpiryHeight is inside the sighash: 0 means no expiry (ZIP 203) and wallets default to 40 blocks (~50 min), which a slow signing round can outlive; muster's spend refuses 0 so invariant 2 holds. frost-rerandomized was excluded from NCC's audit; frost-tools is 'demo only'. reddsa 0.6.0 (2026-09-25) removed its FROST ciphersuites ahead of a move to the frost repo, where they have not landed yet: FROST(Pallas) is only in reddsa <= 0.5.x today. 'refresh' can remove participants; adding one means a new key.

muster.why: the privacy flagship: nothing about the group or the action is visible on-chain. Blocked on tooling maturity, not on muster.

unverified: which crate carries FROST(Pallas) and its EvenY step after reddsa 0.6.0 (announced: ZcashFoundation/frost; absent at main 0966bd15)

families.name: Penumbra threshold custody
families.signs: the effect hash (chain_id, expiry_height, fee, per-action hashes); each follower recomputes it from the TransactionPlan
bypasses: every participant has full view
families.notes: The closest existing model to muster's re-derive-then-sign: followers recompute the effect hash from the plan. No coordination server — copy-paste over a messenger.

muster.why: Penumbra Labs shut down (~Sept 2025); community-run network. The design is worth copying regardless.

families.name: Monero multisig
families.signs: pre-MLSAG hash (prefix + RingCT base + proofs); no chain id, no expiry
families.notes: Setup is N-M+1 key-exchange rounds; info must be re-exchanged after every spend, so transactions are serial.

muster.why: upstream marks it experimental and warns a malicious member can steal funds

families.name: Aztec account contract with multiple signers
families.signs: poseidon2 authwit over (account, chain_id, version, AppPayload hash)
families.notes: The threshold check runs inside a private proof. No first-party multisig account exists. fee_payment_method sits outside the signed hash.

muster.why: a critical proving-system vulnerability was disclosed 2026-08-07 for Alpha V5; fix planned for V6

families.name: Off-chain threshold ECDSA/EdDSA (MPC: CGGMP, DKLs23)
families.signs: whatever digest the target chain needs, so binding, ordering and expiry are that chain's own: the recorded explicit / sequence / none are EVM's (a typed or EIP-155 transaction names the chain id; one account nonce); a Bitcoin spend is implicit / utxo (BIP-143 names the coins spent, not the network)
bypasses: the policy cannot be audited on-chain: whoever runs the policy engine is trusted
families.notes: GG18/GG20 are deprecated (BitForge, TSSHOCK). CVE-2025-66017 (altered presignatures): cggmp21 <= 0.6.3 has no patched release; fixed in cggmp24 0.7.0-alpha.2. Several vendors moved from MPC to TEEs. Open libraries: LFDT-Lockness's cggmp21 repo now ships cggmp24 (no key refresh, no identifiable abort), dkls23 (non-commercial licence; refresh audited, quorum change not audited), cb-mpc (MIT; refresh keeps the same key). The reshare row (new signers, same address) rests on dkls23's unaudited quorum change alone; CGGMP's own refresh is proactive (same party set). Round count is protocol-dependent (CGGMP: 3-round presign + 1 online).

muster.why: a chain-agnostic aggregate that looks single-sig everywhere, including chains without Schnorr. Muster is not production code, so prototype-grade libraries are acceptable now (decision 2026-09-23). PRODUCTION GATE: before real transactions and users, re-choose the library for license, CVE history and identifiable abort.

unverified: whether cb-mpc refresh_ac can move a key to a new access structure (a reshare) or only re-deal it to the same parties

families.name: LEZ public transaction witness set (all of n)
families.signs: SHA256("/LEE/v0.3/Message/Public/" NUL-padded to 32 bytes || borsh{program_account_id, shard_selectors, nonces, instruction_data, fee}) at LEZ v0.3.0, which the public testnet runs since 2026-09-30 (lez/tx.nim held to v0.3.0's own crates, exo-eb6.4); v0.2.4 signed borsh{program_id, account_ids, nonces, instruction_data} under the same prefix. Neither names a chain or zone
families.notes: Every listed signer must sign — many signers, not k-of-n. Separation rests on per-account nonces plus the program id.

muster.why: the trivial n-of-n on Logos; mostly useful as the base the aggregate path builds on

families.name: LEZ multisig program (logos-co/lez-multisig)
families.signs: each member's own LEZ transaction (Propose / Approve / Reject / Execute)
bypasses: the executor supplies the target accounts at execute; a proposal records only their count (logos-co/lez-multisig#40, open)
families.notes: Modelled on Squads v4. Members must be fresh nonce-0 accounts the program claims. At most 10 members. Timelock is future work. On LEZ v0.2.4 a vote was the member's own transaction and cost no fee: its public message had no fee field. The public testnet runs v0.3.0 since 2026-09-30, where every public transaction declares and pays a fee (FeeDeclaration), so per-vote is now a charge; the program's v0.3 port is exo-eb6.4 L4.
families.exposure: LEZ public messages commit to no zone/chain id: a vote transaction is bound only by the member's account nonce and the program id. Muster's envelope binds the environment in the room (invariant 2); the chain does not — the card must say so, and an upstream domain tag is the fix.

muster.why: the vote locus runs live (exo-3c9): lez_multisig_live_e2e drives the room against the program deployed on the public LEZ testnet (ImageID 2ced3d30…d4c7, logos-co/lez-multisig#45) and a local v0.2.4 sequencer. Members' own Propose / Approve transactions are signed by keystore-derived member keys (lez/tx.nim, held to LEZ's own bytes), with an S5 re-read before every vote; settlement counts the votes on chain and Executes; a substituted recipient is refused on the live chain. The hosted surface sends without waiting on a block and completes on inclusion. The published count-only c45100b stays modelled, with #40 named on the card.

families.name: LEZ private multisig (LP-0002 λPrize)
families.signs: each member proves membership and publishes a nullifier per approval over proposal_ref (multisig_id, config_hash, proposal_id, action_hash)
families.notes: Hides WHICH members approved; the threshold, recipient and amount stay public.

muster.why: prize submissions are unofficial and under evaluation

families.name: LEZ public account owned by a FROST key
families.signs: the LEZ public message hash, signed by an aggregate BIP-340 key
families.exposure: LEZ public messages commit to no zone/chain id: a signature by the group's account is bound only by the account's nonce and the program. Muster's envelope binds the environment in the room (invariant 2); the chain does not, and a signature for an old nonce can never land — the card must say so, and an upstream domain tag is the fix.
families.notes: VERIFIED on a LEZ v0.2.4 chain (module/tests/lez_frost_account_e2e.nim, exo-a50.4.6): a public account's id is SHA-256("/LEE/v0.3/AccountId/Public/" ‖ x-only key) and the chain checks a BIP-340 signature under that key, so the x-only form of a ChillDKG threshold key owns an account directly, with no tweak. PrivateKey::tweak (sk + SHA256(pk)) is a wallet-side key derivation the chain never checks. A FROST aggregate co-signed a mint and alone signed a transfer; a wrong aggregate was refused at submission (InvalidSignature). VERIFIED again on a LEZ v0.3.0 chain (module/tests/lez_frost_v030_e2e.nim, exo-eb6.4 L3), where every transaction pays a fee: the account alone sent native LEZ and paid its own fee (2_968 against a 134_400_000 cap), a keystore member co-signed as the group's fee payer, and a wrong aggregate moved nothing.

muster.why: the same FROST-secp256k1 group as btc.frost-bip445 gives Logos a threshold account that looks single-sig: the ADR-015 aggregate-signature rail on our own chain. An aggregate key owns a public account untweaked (lez_frost_account_e2e), and the room drives it end to end on a real v0.2.4 chain (lez_frost_room_e2e): a ceremony on a lez: zone discloses the account, a lez-call at the account's chain-read nonce runs both rounds, and settlement re-reads the nonce, aggregates one signature and sends it; a stale nonce is refused. On LEZ v0.3.0 the same room path runs with a lez-call v2 effect, the group paying its own fee (lez_frost_room_v030_e2e). Hosted and in the room UI (open a lez: ceremony, the transfer composer, Approve once). Demo-grade (not constant time), behind the production gate.

families.name: Split a bill, settled on an EVM chain
families.signs: the agreement: each debtor's room key (Ed25519) over dCBOR [domain, schema, chain, asset, total, creditor, payTo, shares, memo]; the settlement: each debtor's own EIP-155 transfer of their share to payTo
families.notes: No shared account: one member fronted a bill, the split names every debtor and their share, and each debtor pays their own share from their own wallet. The room holds the agreement; nothing on the chain counts or enforces it, so settlement is motivational — the card names each person who owes. Every payment is an ordinary transfer: payer, payee and amount are public, and several payments to one address close together link the group. Muster never tags a payment on-chain with the split (that would publish the group); the link between a payment and a share lives in the room.

muster.why: the driver, the parts seam and the room fold are built and conform (split_driver_test, parts_fold_test): the threshold is every debtor the effect names, only a named debtor's room key agrees, each debtor settles their own part and only the creditor confirms it, the payment is derived from the agreed effect. Paying from the member's own wallet and the creditor's confirmation from her own RPC read run end to end on anvil (split_anvil_e2e); the hosted methods (coordinate_propose_split / settle_part / confirm_part) are wired, and the UI (the Split composer and card) is driven end to end through the real runner by scripts/split-self-test.sh. The composer and card were looked at on a display (Xvfb) through a whole split and fixed (exo-9a4). A share may be paid in ETH or an ERC-20 token (erc20:<0x token>): transfer() on the token, confirmed from its Transfer log (split_erc20_anvil_e2e, exo-5ab).

families.name: Split a bill privately on the LEZ (shielded payee, private rail)
families.signs: the agreement: each debtor's room key (Ed25519) over the split's dCBOR; the settlement: each debtor's own private transfer (private rail) to the creditor's shielded key node
families.exposure: LEZ public messages commit to no zone/chain id (see lez.multisig-program); whether a privacy-preserving transfer commits to one is unverified. Muster binds the environment in the room (invariant 2); the card must say whether the chain does.
families.notes: The private split: payTo must be a shielded key node and each debtor pays on the private rail, so the chain names no payer, payee or amount (docs/design/lez-adapter.md, the four rails). The creditor confirms by scan: a private note carries no payer or transaction link, so every share of a private split is a DIFFERENT amount (a few base units apart, the creditor absorbing them) and a note is matched to its share by that exact amount, at payTo, claimed once. The room records a hash of the note's id, never the note.

muster.why: the educational payoff of the split: the same agreement as evm.split, and the chain learns nothing that links the group. Built and tested on a shared fake chain (split_lez_test): a shielded payTo, every share a distinct amount, debtors pay shielded → shielded only (a public source is refused), and the creditor's own scan confirms a part only when a note of exactly that share arrived at payTo and is not already claimed. Hosted and in the UI, and run end to end on the LEZ testnet across two instances with real lez_core wallets (scripts/split-lez-testnet.sh, 2026-09-28): the debtor paid privately, the creditor's own scan found a note of exactly the share, final on both. The composer and card were looked at on a display (Xvfb) through a whole private split, and fixed (exo-9a4).

unverified: whether a LEZ privacy-preserving transaction commits to a zone/chain id

families.name: Split a bill, settled in Bitcoin
families.signs: the agreement: each debtor's room key (Ed25519) over dCBOR [domain, schema, chain, asset, total, creditor, payTo, shares, memo]; the settlement: each debtor's own single-key Bitcoin spend (P2WPKH, DER over BIP-143) paying payTo their share
families.notes: The split, paid in BTC: each debtor pays their share in satoshis from their own key — wpkh of their muster key, coins read from their own node — and the creditor's own node confirms a payment when an output pays payTo exactly the share at the network's confirmation depth. Every payment is an ordinary Bitcoin transaction: its inputs name the payer, and payee and amount are public once broadcast; the coins it spends bind it to one chain. No share may be below the 546-sat dust limit. Muster never tags a payment on-chain with the split; the link lives in the room.

muster.why: the third split family (exo-d17): the same driver, the parts seam and a Bitcoin part seam (coordination/parts_btc.nim). Built and held without a node (split_btc_test: BIP-173's P2WPKH vector, every input signed by the payer's key over BIP-143, the creditor's exact-output match, dust and network refusals) and end to end on a real Bitcoin Core regtest (split_btc_regtest_e2e: two debtors pay from their own coins, a one-satoshi-short payment and one to someone else are refused, the creditor's own node confirms both, final on all three). Hosted (coordinate_propose_split on a bip122 chain, settle / confirm through the member's own node).
